answer: Urban land use is differentially associated with the three introduction pathways. At the local (plot) scale, urban land use is most strongly linked to the Unintentional pathway: plots adjacent to urban areas carry a higher proportional share of their invasive species from accidental introductions (contaminated seed lots, trade, tourism) — adjusted binomial OR ≈ 1.12 per +10% urban cover within 500 m (p ≈ 0.05; p = 0.004 without the habitat covariate; p = 0.072 at the 1000 m buffer; unadjusted chi-square of pathway composition, high- vs low-urban plots, p = 0.004; Urban-habitat plots, p = 0.006) — and these are short, wide-niche weedy generalists (mean height 1.1 m, invaded niche breadth 0.75, in 9.6 plots on average). In the same adjusted models, Gardening (ornamental) introductions are associated with LESS urban exposure, in both the proportional share (OR ≈ 0.88, p ≈ 0.04) and absolute per-plot counts (IRR ≈ 0.93, p ≈ 0.03) — a genuine partial effect, not a raw contrast — while AgriForest (agriculture/forestry) introductions show no detectable urban association (all p ≥ 0.07). At the regional scale, the Gardening pathway is the one that surged in step with urbanization: its share of recorded introductions rose from 41% (pre-1985) to 75% in 1985-2019 (period × pathway chi-square p < 1e-46), the era in which urban cover in plot buffers tripled (1956→2009). So: urbanization-era introductions are dominated by Gardening/ornamental introductions regionally, while locally urban land use shifts invaded assemblages toward Unintentional, trade-mediated weedy species; AgriForest introductions are not urban-linked.

payload.workflow: Inspected 4 files (632 plots; 81 species; 4x3 period x pathway table; 79-tip phylogeny). Binomial GLMs of per-plot pathway share (n_p of n_total) on urban_2009_500m with habitat, elevation, temperature, rainfall, distance to road/stream, cropland as covariates; robustness via no-habitat, urban-only, and all 9 urban buffer-year + change variables. Poisson GLMs (HC3) for absolute per-plot counts. Chi-square tests: high- vs low-urban composition, Urban vs other habitats, invasion probability, period x pathway. Species traits compared by pathway. All code in analysis.py; output in results.txt.
